fact: ANPTIC states it hosts the administration's business software, websites and collaborative platforms in public-administration data centres and runs a cloud IaaS portal with 492 virtual machines created for government structures (undated page, published date used).

ANPTIC lists under its own 'services and applications developed' the government systems Bondoo, Tawale, Toumnana (SIGED), SIGEPE, Helpdesk and e-conseil des ministres (undated page, published date used).
The ANAGRASC claims-registration platform was designed with the help of ANPTIC, the state ICT agency, and launched on 3 September 2026.

Profile states that as ANPTIC director of operations and technical support he oversaw operation of RESINA, the government network, and the administration's institutional messaging platforms; no date given, published date used.

The ANPTIC-run government cloud portal states it hosts 139 websites and 622 virtual machines, connects 354 communes and offers SaaS business applications (SIGASPE, CID, CIFE, CIE, e-conseil des ministres) to government; figures undated, capture date used.

The profile states that from 2007 an engineer in the government's Direction generale chargee de la coordination des programmes TIC led the maintenance, extension and reinforcement of RESINA, the national administration network, including fibre backbone, WiMAX stations, servers, IP telephony, DNS and DHCP; no end date is given, and the date is the start of his service there.
The ANPTIC director general is reported as recalling that the E-conseil (paperless Council of Ministers) was set up thanks to ANPTIC; no date is given for it, so the article's published date is used.
The Treasury's director general said Lanaya and e-BDT were developed by the Treasury's own administration (not a contractor), and they were officially launched on 3 April 2026 in Ouagadougou.
The Treasury's own administration, not a contractor, developed Lanaya.
The Treasury's own administration, not a contractor, developed e-BDT.
